title: Stri: Gandhari's curse
hook: at the river, with water in their hands for the dead, Kunti finally tells her sons who Karna was
tomorrow: Shanti and Anushasana: Bhishma's teachings from the bed of arrows (selections)

segments.voice: Yesterday in Stri, Gandhari cursed Krishna, and he took the curse without striking back. Your line was he takes it without striking back.

Water is the last thing the living can give the dead. After the fires on the field are lit, the whole household walks down to the Ganga: the Pandavas, Dhritarashtra, Gandhari, Kunti, the widows of both sides. One by one they step into the river and offer water for each person they lost, a father, a brother, a son, a teacher. A quiet, orderly rite after so much noise. And in the middle of it, Kunti tells her sons something she has carried their whole lives.
screen: `THE FIRES ARE LIT.` → `EVERYONE GOES TO THE GANGA.` → `KUNTI SPEAKS.`

segments.voice: Kunti asks her sons to offer water for one more warrior: Karna. The brothers are puzzled. Karna was the enemy, the charioteer's son, the man Arjuna killed. Why him? He was your eldest brother, Kunti tells them. My son, born to me from the sun god before I married your father. I set him adrift as a baby, and I never told you. The Pandavas are stunned. Yudhishthira is crushed. Soon after, as the next book opens, he remembers how Karna's feet resembled Kunti's, the text says, and how his anger used to drain away when he looked at them. Now he understands why. He grieves for the brother he fought without knowing, who, he realizes, could have been on his side all along. He offers the water for Karna himself, and brings Karna's family into the rites. The book of the women opened with a blind king's grief. It closes with a woman's word changing what the men thought the war was. Gandhari held back a curse, then spoke one. The widows walked the field. And at the river, Kunti turns the victory upside down: the warrior whose fall they had cheered was their own brother. That's Stri, a book where the women speak, and the winners learn what their victory cost.
screen: `"OFFER WATER FOR KARNA"` · `"HE WAS YOUR ELDEST BROTHER"` · `YUDHISHTHIRA REMEMBERS HIS FEET` · then, large: `THE WOMEN SPEAK LAST`

segments.voice: Cup your hands in your lap as if holding a little water, and bring to mind someone you've lost, or someone you're no longer close to. Breathe in and remember one true thing about them; breathe out and let your hands stay open, as if offering it back, along with anything you never said or never knew. If you pray, you can hold them in your prayer.
Stri. Woman. The book that ends at the river, with water for the dead and Kunti's secret about Karna.
Your line: he was your eldest brother. Tomorrow, Yudhishthira goes to Bhishma on the bed of arrows. Day eight hundred sixty, done.

screen: `DAY 860 COUNTS.` → `TOMORROW: SHANTI AND ANUSHASANA: BHISHMA'S TEACHINGS FROM THE BED OF ARROWS (SELECTIONS).`

howItsDone: Hindu rites after a death can include offering water for the dead, often at a river, and retellings of the Mahabharata return to the moment at the Ganga when Kunti names Karna as her son.

notes: All paraphrase. Confirm in Ganguli that Kunti reveals Karna at the water offerings at the close of the Stri Parva, and the wording 'born from the sun god before I married'.
Yudhishthira's memory of Karna's feet resembling Kunti's: in some editions this appears at the start of the Shanti Parva rather than the end of the Stri Parva. Confirm placement.
Confirm that Yudhishthira brings Karna's family (wives/household) into the rites.

Audit: the Stri Parva opens with Dhritarashtra's grief and Vidura's counsel (days 855-856), not a woman's grief; the false 'ends where it began' line was rewritten.
